subject.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns

question: Should durable browser-tab rows be retired after 24 hours of genuine unavailable-browser cleanup failures, accepting that a same-instance browser returning later will no longer be tracked for cleanup?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent and proof-backed, but the correct retention horizon is a product compatibility decision: it balances self-healing capacity against eventual cleanup for long-offline user browsers.

options.title: Adopt bounded retirement
options.body: Merge the 24-hour retirement policy to prevent unreachable rows from permanently consuming the capped durable store.

options.title: Preserve indefinite retry
options.body: Keep the existing retry-forever behavior and pursue a separately approved capacity or operator-recovery design without dropping durable rows by age.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded retirement
recommendation.body: Merge the 24-hour retirement policy to prevent unreachable rows from permanently consuming the capped durable store.

likelyOwner.reason: FMLS introduced the current durable ownership and cleanup model in the merged restart-cleanup work, so they are best positioned to confirm its intended long-outage contract.
